The diagram and tables below show the validation rules applied to the input to the Julia core before running the model.
Some node types have more complex connectivity validation than shown here.
See the [Junction](node/junction.qmd) and [UserDemand](node/user-demand.qmd) pages for their additional rules.

# Allowed connectivity

The diagram below shows every allowed upstream and downstream node type for each node type that can have flow links.
Each group has its own nodes, with upstream neighbors on the left, downstream neighbors on the right, and flow directed from left to right.
This is a connectivity illustration, not a valid simulation model.

```{python}
# | code-fold: true
# | fig-width: 5
# | fig-height: 30
from unittest.mock import patch

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.offsetbox import AnnotationBbox
from ribasim import Model, Node
from ribasim.geometry.link import LinkTable
from ribasim.node_icons import make_icon_box
from ribasim.utils import _pascal_to_snake
from ribasim.validation import link_neighbor_amount, node_type_connectivity
from shapely.geometry import Point

model = Model(starttime="2020-01-01", endtime="2020-01-02", crs="EPSG:28992")
flow_node_types = [
    node_type
    for node_type, bounds in link_neighbor_amount["flow"].items()
    if bounds[1] > 0 or bounds[3] > 0
]
central_ids = set()
upstream_ids = set()

with patch.object(LinkTable, "_validate_link", return_value=None):
    for i, node_type in enumerate(flow_node_types):
        x = 0
        y = -i * 8
        central = getattr(model, _pascal_to_snake(node_type)).add(
            Node(geometry=Point(x, y), name=node_type)
        )
        central_ids.add(central.node_id)
        upstream_types = [
            upstream_type
            for upstream_type in flow_node_types
            if node_type in node_type_connectivity[upstream_type]
        ]
        downstream_types = node_type_connectivity[node_type]
        for direction, neighbor_types in [(-1, upstream_types), (1, downstream_types)]:
            for j, neighbor_type in enumerate(neighbor_types):
                neighbor_y = y + ((len(neighbor_types) - 1) / 2 - j) * 0.7
                neighbor = getattr(model, _pascal_to_snake(neighbor_type)).add(
                    Node(geometry=Point(x + direction * 3, neighbor_y), name=neighbor_type)
                )
                if direction == -1:
                    upstream_ids.add(neighbor.node_id)
                    model.link.add(neighbor, central)
                else:
                    model.link.add(central, neighbor)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 30))
model.plot(ax=ax, indicate_subnetworks=False, aspect_ratio_bound=0.05)
ax.set_aspect("auto")
ax.get_legend().remove()
for artist in list(ax.artists):
    if isinstance(artist, AnnotationBbox):
        artist.remove()
for text in list(ax.texts):
    text.remove()
for node_id, node in model.node.df.iterrows():
    is_central = node_id in central_ids
    is_upstream = node_id in upstream_ids
    ax.add_artist(
        AnnotationBbox(
            make_icon_box(node["node_type"], size=44),
            (node.geometry.x, node.geometry.y),
            frameon=False,
            pad=0,
            zorder=3,
        )
    )
    ax.annotate(
        node["name"],
        xy=(node.geometry.x, node.geometry.y),
        xytext=(0, 28) if is_central else (-28 if is_upstream else 28, 0),
        textcoords="offset points",
        ha="center" if is_central else ("right" if is_upstream else "left"),
        va="bottom" if is_central else "center",
        fontsize=9,
        fontweight="bold" if is_central else "normal",
    )
ax.axis("off")
plt.show()
plt.close(fig)
```

# Neighbor amounts

The tables below show the minimum and maximum numbers of incoming and outgoing neighbors for each node type, per link type.
`∞` means there is no upper bound.

```{python}
# | code-fold: true
# | output: asis
from ribasim.validation import link_neighbor_amount


for link_type in ("flow", "control", "listen"):
    node_bounds = link_neighbor_amount[link_type]
    print(f"\n## {link_type.title()} links\n")
    print("| Node type | in_min | in_max | out_min | out_max |")
    print("|:----------|-------:|-------:|--------:|--------:|")
    for node_type, bounds in node_bounds.items():
        values = ["∞" if value == 2**63 - 1 else str(value) for value in bounds]
        print(f"| {node_type} | {' | '.join(values)} |")
    print()
```

::: {.callout-note}
Pump and Outlet can receive two control links, in which case one must be from a FlowDemand, and the other from a control node.
:::
